title: Exhaustion call sites (webhook delivery-failure + wrong-person route) have no direct tests — only the SQL primitives are pinned
detail: Round guard 4 (exhaustion LIVE at BOTH failure sites) is only partially traced. server/test/integration/reference_checks_actions_integration_test.gleam:491 (second_failure_exhausts_to_unreachable_with_signal_test) drives rc_sql.exhaust_reference_call + rc_sql.stamp_referee_contact_invalid directly — the SQL mechanism — but neither of the two LIVE call sites is exercised: server/src/reference_checks/webhooks.gleam:437 (exhaust_row, the resend/SMS delivery-failure branch on row.correction_cycles >= 1) and server/src/reference_checks/form_handler.gleam:1262 (exhaust_wrong_person) have zero tests. Consequently the reference_call_correction_exhausted audit event (write_exhaustion_audit), the in-app notification notify_reference_correction_exhausted (notification_dispatch.gleam), the minimal_terminal_result attempt-log carry, and the response path are asserted nowhere. The first-failure boundary (no exhaust) is covered by pre-existing webhook/exit-routes tests on fresh rows, so the branch flip itself is the gap: a wiring defect in either call site (wrong audit event, dropped notification, broken exhaust SQL call) would ship green. The integration file's own header comment says 'this is what the webhook/wrong-person call sites run' — an acknowledgment that the call sites themselves are bypassed.
recommended_fix: Add integration tests that drive the two call sites end-to-end: (a) a svix-verified Resend bounce (or Twilio failure) on a row with correction_cycles = 1 asserting status unreachable + referee_contact_invalid stamped + reference_call_correction_exhausted audit row + reference_unreachable in-app notification; (b) a POST /reference/:token/wrong-person on a corrected row asserting the same (mirroring reference_exit_routes_integration_test.gleam's wrong-person helpers, with correction_cycles bumped first). Also assert the first failure on a corrected row still does NOT exhaust.

title: RC4.3 panel state is not reset on route change despite the model comment promising it — stale confirm/edit state (incl. typed referee PII) leaks across applicants and no test covers the reset
detail: client/src/model.gleam documents refcheck_menu_open/refcheck_confirm/refcheck_edit/refcheck_action_inflight as 'All reset on route change (they are per-application surfaces)', but neither reset site does it: the BrowserChangedUrl handler (client/src/client.gleam:457) and the ApplicationDetail branch of it (client.gleam:650-665) reset refcheck_expanded, refcheck_explainer_open, viewing_popover_open, report_download_loading, insight_expanded, confirm_action, show_approval_confirm etc. — not the four RC4.3 fields. ApiReturnedApplicationDetail (client.gleam:2981+) likewise resets documents_expanded/show_all_audit but not the RC4.3 surfaces. Consequence: a pending take-over/start inline confirm or an open §8.3 edit-trio (with the landlord's typed referee name/email/phone held in model.refcheck_edit) survives navigation to another applicant and re-renders when the landlord returns to the same application; refcheck_action_inflight also carries stale ids. This contradicts the codebase's explicit per-application reset pattern and the model's own comment. No client test pins the reset (the existing refcheck_route_change_resets_expanded_rows_test only covers the RC4.2 fields).
recommended_fix: Add refcheck_menu_open: None, refcheck_confirm: None, refcheck_edit: None, refcheck_action_inflight: set.new() to the ApplicationDetail route-change branch (and/or the BrowserChangedUrl reset block) in client/src/client.gleam, and extend the route-change reset test in client/test/client_test.gleam to assert all four fields clear.

title: Em-dash ban unenforced for the new refcheck copy — 5 implementer-authored toasts and the attempt-log export ship em-dashes past the guard, and the new CtxRefcheckAction context is missing from copy_test's all_contexts
detail: Round guard 9 + carried warning 2 (no_em_dash_test doesn't scan refcheck copy): client/test/copy_test.gleam:296 for_each_copy only iterates copy.toast(code, ctx) and copy.page(code, ctx) outputs, so the RC4.3 constants in client/src/copy.gleam are never scanned by no_em_dash_test (line 308). Five new implementer-authored toasts (no UX-spec verbatim source — the spec fixes no toast copy for these) contain the banned em-dash: copy.gleam:874 'Reference started — the invite goes out now.', :878 'Reference re-enabled — it's back in the queue.', :880 'You're handling this one — automated messages stopped.', :882 'Details saved — the invitation is on its way again.', :884 'Referee substituted — the new invitation is on its way.' The new timeline composition site client/src/client.gleam:6772 (build_attempt_log_text, the §7.7 attempt-log export) also joins with ' — ' (attempt.at <> ' — ' <> channel <> ' — ' <> outcome), i.e. em-dashes in implementer-authored user-facing text. Separately, copy_test.gleam:50 all_contexts() omits the new copy.CtxRefcheckAction variant — violating the file's own convention ('If a new variant is added upstream, adding it here produces a test failure') — so the three new context-specific toast arms (NotFound/Conflict/VacancyUnavailable x CtxRefcheckAction) are exercised by the totality/em-dash/forbidden-word scans only via the generic wildcard, and no test pins their specific copy (unlike conflict_on_status_update_mentions_shortlisted_test for other contexts). The implementer's green-CI claim holds only because the guard never sees the new strings.
recommended_fix: Replace the em-dashes in the five toasts and the attempt-log export joins with the house style (plain commas/periods), add CtxRefcheckAction to all_contexts() in client/test/copy_test.gleam, and extend for_each_copy (or add a scan over the refcheck copy constants) so no_em_dash_test and no_forbidden_words_test cover the panel's new strings.

title: HTTP-level coverage of the new endpoints is thin: take-over, substitute and the ?slot= start variant are only tested below the handler
detail: Of the four new/changed server surfaces, only correct is driven through its HTTP handler: reference_checks_actions_integration_test.gleam:392-413 (correct_validation_and_cross_application_guards_test exercises handle_correct over wisp/simulate — validation 400s + cross-tenant 404). take-over and substitute are tested exclusively via actions_handler.do_take_over / do_substitute (DB-level), leaving untested: the two new router arms (server/src/router.gleam take-over/correct/substitute POST arms), require_json's malformed-body 400 for those endpoints, take-over's read_owned_row 404-vs-409 split over HTTP, and the archived-vacancy 422 branch of the new run_action_with_prechecks copy (the trigger's own archived-422 test covers trigger's copy, not this one — reference_checks_trigger_integration_test.gleam:583). Similarly the per-slot start is tested by calling run_create_checks_slot directly (reference_checks_actions_integration_test.gleam:735); handle_start's new ?slot= parsing (slot_query) and the invalid-slot 400 are untested. All guarded logic is pinned at the SQL/do_* level, so this is a wiring-level gap, not a logic gap.
recommended_fix: Add wisp/simulate HTTP tests for handle_take_over and handle_substitute (malformed body 400, cross-tenant 404, wrong-pre-state 409, archived 422), and a handle_start test with ?slot=employer_ref plus an invalid-slot 400.

title: Client handler tests don't cover the confirm→fire and save→fire paths — the 'actions actually fire' traceability is partial
detail: Round item 6 (client tests: menu dispatch / actions actually fire): client/test/client_test.gleam pins menu toggle, start-choice-opens-confirm, skip immediate-fire (inflight mark), edit-trio live values, the two validation blocks, and the API-response toast handling (8 tests). Missing from client.update coverage: UserConfirmedRefcheckAction for BOTH kinds (start → start_check with the row's slot; take-over → take_over_reference), UserSavedRefcheckEdit with a valid trio (correct/substitute → fire), the re-enable handler path, and UserClickedRefcheckExport (attempt-log clipboard + AppCompletedRefcheckExport). Panel render tests (reference_panel_test.gleam) cover the surfaces (queued/skipped menus, start/take-over confirms, taken-over block, correction trio, objected substitute, inflight disable) but not the unreachable-row menu (Take over + Substitute entries) or the contact_initiated menu. The wiring is thin and server-guarded, so no blocker — but the RC4.2 guard-flip (menu must actually dispatch) is only half-pinned.
recommended_fix: Add client.update tests: confirm start fires (inflight marked), confirm take-over fires, valid save fires correct/substitute (inflight marked), re-enable fires; add panel render assertions for the unreachable and contact_initiated overflow menus.

title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
detail: P0 100%: the three load-bearing guards are fully pinned — take-over guard matrix + taken_over_at/clock clear + sweep exclusion (take_over_row_is_excluded_from_the_sweep_test) + §8.6 late completion (taken_over_row_can_still_complete_late_test); correct one-cycle incl. snapshot immutability + correction_cycles=1 + re-arm + audit + second-correct 409 (correct_is_guarded_on_awaiting_correction_test); substitute idempotency (exactly 2 rows + exactly 1 audit on double-submit) + old/new ids in audit; expand-only migration with back-compat decoder (detail_decoder_tolerates_missing_rc43_keys_test) and untouched strip assertions. P1 ~80-89%: exhaustion call-site wiring (webhook + wrong-person routes, audit event, notification) untested; client confirm→fire/save→fire paths untested; em-dash/forbidden-word scan doesn't cover the new refcheck copy and CtxRefcheckAction is missing from copy_test all_contexts. Overall coverage >= 80%. Claimed counts verified against the tree: 514 integration (claimed 512), 540 client (exact), 110 shared (exact), 1474 server unit (claimed 1476).
recommended_fix: To reach PASS: add the two exhaustion call-site integration tests (webhook + wrong-person with correction_cycles >= 1, asserting stamp + reference_call_correction_exhausted audit + in-app notification), add CtxRefcheckAction to all_contexts and scan the refcheck copy constants in the em-dash/forbidden-word tests, and pin the client confirm/save fire paths.
